summary: This is the Wikipedia infobox-style summary of the Wimbledon gentlemen's singles tournament, held at the AELTC in London since 1877 on grass. The note gives basic tournament details, including 132 editions overall, 50 in the Open Era since 1968, and 2017 prize money of £2,200,000. It also lists the most titles and most consecutive titles in the amateur and Open eras, along with the current champion, Novak Djokovic, who has four titles.
one_line: Overview of the Wimbledon gentlemen's singles tournament, its editions, prize money, and record title holders.
key_facts: The Wimbledon Gentlemen's Singles tournament is located in London, United Kingdom.
The venue and governing body of the Wimbledon Gentlemen's Singles is the AELTC.
The tournament has been staged for 132 editions.
The Open Era of the tournament began in 1968 and has 50 editions.
The tournament surface is grass, used from 1877 to the present.
The prize money for the Wimbledon Gentlemen's Singles was £2,200,000 in 2017.
The trophy for the tournament is the Gentleman's Singles Trophy.
William Renshaw holds the amateur era record for most titles with 7, won in the challenge round.
Fred Perry has 3 amateur era titles, won in the regular format.
Roger Federer holds the Open era record for most titles with 8.
William Renshaw holds the amateur era record for most consecutive titles with 6, won in the challenge round.
Björn Borg and Roger Federer each hold the Open era record for most consecutive titles with 5.
Novak Djokovic is the current champion, with his fourth title.
